declarations.RDF11.Set: A set is represented by a membership proposition for each possible element. It has no positions, order or duplicate occurrences.
declarations.RDF11.Set.empty: The empty set contains no elements: every membership proposition is false.
declarations.RDF11.Set.singleton: The singleton containing a consists exactly of elements equal to a.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union: An element belongs to the union when it belongs to either input set.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset: s is a subset of t when every member of s is also a member of t.
declarations.RDF11.Set.image: An element belongs to the image when some original member is mapped to it. Several originals may have the same image.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ofList: Interpret a list by membership alone. Repeated occurrences do not create additional set members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ext: Two sets are equal if every element belongs to one exactly when it belongs to the other. The proof uses equality of propositions and functions.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_idempotent: Taking the union of a set with itself gives exactly the same set.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_comm: Swapping the two sets in a union does not change its members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_assoc: Regrouping three unions does not change their members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset_refl: Every set is a subset of itself.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset_trans: If every member of s is in t, and every member of t is in u, then every member of s is in u.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ofList_repeat: The list [a, a] and the list [a] denote exactly the same set.
declarations.RDF11.Term: An RDF term has exactly one of three tagged forms: IRI, literal, or blank node. The tags keep the categories distinct even if their underlying representations coincide. The concrete IRI and literal domains remain abstract.
declarations.RDF11.Subject: An ordinary RDF subject is an IRI or a blank node. There is no literal constructor, so a literal subject cannot be constructed at this type.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.toTerm: View an admissible ordinary subject as a general RDF term, preserving its IRI or blank-node identity.
declarations.RDF11.Triple: An ordinary triple has three fields: an IRI-or-blank subject, an IRI predicate, and any RDF term as object. The field types enforce these position restrictions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple: A generalized triple allows an IRI, literal or blank node in any of its three positions. This is wider syntax than an ordinary RDF triple.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize: Embed an ordinary triple into generalized syntax without changing any of its three RDF terms.
declarations.RDF11.Graph: An ordinary RDF graph is a set of ordinary triples. Duplicate membership and triple order are not extra graph data; the definition does not assume a finite graph.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph: A generalized graph is a set of generalized triples. It retains set identity while allowing the wider triple syntax.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize: Embed every ordinary triple of a graph into generalized syntax, taking the set of the resulting triples.
declarations.RDF11.Term.hasBlank: Test whether this term is the specified blank node; IRIs and literals do not contain blank nodes.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.hasBlank: A blank node occurs in a generalized triple if it occupies any one of its three positions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.hasBlank: A blank node occurs in a graph if at least one member triple contains it.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.ground: A graph is ground when no blank node occurs in it.
declarations.RDF11.Term.hasLiteral: Test whether a term is the specified literal.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.hasLiteral: The specified literal occurs if it occupies at least one position of this generalized triple.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank: Apply f to blank-node identities, leaving every IRI and literal unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank: Apply the same blank-node mapping to all three positions of this triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank: Apply the same blank-node mapping throughout the graph and collect the resulting triples as a set.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank_id: Leaving each blank-node identity unchanged leaves every term unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank_comp: Renaming a term first by f and then by h equals renaming once by the composite function h after f.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank_id: Identity blank renaming leaves the entire triple unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank_comp: Two successive blank renamings of a triple equal one composed renaming.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_id: Identity blank renaming leaves the graph equal as a set.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation: A simple interpretation packages IR (resources), IP (properties), IEXT (property extensions), IS (IRI denotation) and partial IL (literal denotation). IR is nonempty. IR and IP may overlap; this structure does not assume every property is a resource.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Resource: A resource is an element of the ambient universe together with evidence that it belongs to IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Property: A property is an ambient element together with evidence that it belongs to IP.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Assignment: A blank assignment is a partial function from blank identities to resources. The separate AssignmentOn condition constrains its exact domain for a graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.AssignmentOn: The assignment is defined exactly for the blank nodes occurring in G: every occurring blank gets a resource, and no unused blank does.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote: This is the extended interpretation [I+A]: IRIs use IS, literals use partial IL, and blanks use A. The result may be undefined.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.TripleTrue: A triple is true when its predicate denotes a property, its subject and object denote resources, and that resource pair belongs to the property extension IEXT.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.GraphTrue: With one fixed assignment A, every member triple of G must be true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Satisfies: I satisfies G when there exists one assignment for exactly G’s blank nodes that makes all G’s triples true. The same assignment witnesses the whole graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.restrict: Remove assignment entries for blank nodes that do not occur in G, retaining all entries used by G.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_agrees: Assignments agreeing on the blanks in a term give that term the same denotation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ag: Assignments agreeing on the blanks in a triple give it the same truth value.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_res: Removing assignment entries unused by G does not change whether all its triples are true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_bl: A true triple has a defined resource assignment for every blank node occurring in it.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_iff: To prove satisfaction it is enough to find an assignment making every triple true, even if it initially assigns unused blanks. The proof restricts that assignment to the exact graph domain.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_emp: Every interpretation satisfies the empty graph, since there are no member triples whose truth needs checking.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_sub: An interpretation satisfying G also satisfies any subgraph H: restrict the witnessing assignment to the blanks used by H.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.undefined_lit: A triple with an object literal whose IL value is undefined cannot be true.
A generalized triple with an undefined literal in any position cannot be true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graph_with_un: If a graph has a member triple containing an undefined literal, this interpretation cannot satisfy the graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ground_satisf: For a graph with no blanks, satisfaction is equivalent to truth of every triple under the empty assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimplyEntails: G simply entails E when every simple interpretation satisfying G also satisfies E. The quantification covers every carrier type in an arbitrary fixed Lean universe, not just a finite sample or a particular algorithm.
declarations.RDF11.LogicallyEquivalent: Two graphs are logically equivalent when each simply entails the other.
declarations.RDF11.simplyEntails_refl: Every graph entails itself: the same satisfaction proof is enough.
declarations.RDF11.simplyEntails_trans: Entailment composes: if G entails H and H entails E, G entails E.
declarations.RDF11.subgraph_entailment: Every graph entails each of its subgraphs, because truth of every member triple implies truth of the selected subset.
declarations.RDF11.premise_monotonicity: Adding triples to a premise cannot remove a simple entailment it already had.
declarations.RDF11.entails_empty: Every graph entails the empty graph, which is true in every interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.indiscriminate: This witness interpretation has one resource/property and makes every property pair true; all names denote that same element. It is used to prove existence of a model, not to restrict interpretations generally.
declarations.RDF11.all_graphs_simply_satisfiable: Every graph has a simple model, even if the graph is infinite. The proof uses the one-element indiscriminate interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.noPairs: This one-element interpretation has empty property extensions, so no triple is true. It provides a countermodel when needed.
declarations.RDF11.empty_entails_only_empty: If the empty graph entails E, then E has no triples. Otherwise the interpretation with empty property extensions would refute E while satisfying the empty premise.
declarations.RDF11.EntailsUnder: Entailment under extra conditions C quantifies only over simple interpretations satisfying C, retaining the same graph truth conditions.
declarations.RDF11.extension_preserves_simple_entailm: A simple entailment survives restricting interpretations by additional conditions C.
declarations.RDF11.stronger_conditions_preserve_entai: If every interpretation meeting D also meets C, then every entailment under C is valid under D.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_mapBla: Evaluating a renamed term under A is the same as evaluating the original under the assignment that first follows the renaming.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ma: The same pullback of assignments preserves truth for a renamed triple.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_map: The same pullback of assignments preserves truth of all triples in a renamed graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_map: If I satisfies the graph after a blank-to-blank mapping, then I satisfies the original graph. Pull back the witnessing assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_uni: Under one fixed assignment, a union is true exactly when both component graphs are true under that same assignment.
declarations.RDF11.merge: Merge first places the two graphs’ blank nodes in disjoint left/right domains, then takes the union of their renamed triples. This prevents accidental sharing.
declarations.RDF11.satisfies_merge: I satisfies the merge exactly when I satisfies each graph separately. The separate assignments combine because the renamed blank domains are disjoint.
declarations.RDF11.union_entails_merge: The union entails the merge: one shared assignment that satisfies the union supplies separate witnesses for both graphs.
declarations.RDF11.renamed_entails_original: Every blank-to-blank image of a graph entails the original. The mapping need not be injective, so this includes identification of blanks, not only bijective renaming.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution: A substitution optionally assigns an RDF term to each blank identity. An omitted entry means leave that blank unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution.resolve: Look up a blank’s replacement; if no replacement was specified, return the original blank term.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute: Replace a blank once by its resolved image, leaving names fixed. This is simultaneous substitution: a replacement is not recursively substituted again in the same application.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.substitute: Use one substitution consistently in the subject, predicate and object positions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute: The substituted graph is the set of substituted member triples. If several triples become identical, they are one set member.
declarations.RDF11.IsInstance: H is an instance of G when some substitution produces exactly H from G. In IsInstance H G, H is the result and G is the original.
declarations.RDF11.InstanceWithVocabulary: An instance relative to V uses only names from V when replacing occurring blanks. Names already in G are preserved and need not belong to V.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution.then: Compose two substitutions by applying the second to each resolved image of the first. This represents two successive simultaneous substitutions.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute_id: A substitution with no specified replacements leaves a term unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute_comp: Substituting a term twice equals one application of the composed substitution.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute_id: Leaving every blank unchanged leaves the whole graph unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute_comp: Substituting a graph twice gives the same set as applying the composed substitution once.
declarations.RDF11.instance_refl: Every graph is an instance of itself; use the substitution that leaves every blank unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.instance_trans: An instance of an instance is an instance of the original graph; compose the two substitutions.
declarations.RDF11.instance_triple_origin: Every triple in the substituted graph has at least one original member triple whose substitution produces it.
declarations.RDF11.ProperSubstitution: A substitution is proper for G when it replaces an occurring blank by an IRI or literal, or identifies two distinct occurring blanks. Collisions with an unchanged blank count; unused ambient identities do not.
declarations.RDF11.ProperInstance: H is a proper instance of G when a proper substitution produces it. This does not say H is a proper subgraph of G.
declarations.RDF11.LeanGraph: A graph is lean when every instance that is also a subgraph equals the graph itself. Thus no instance is a proper subgraph. This is RDF leanness, not the proof assistant’s name.
declarations.RDF11.ground_substitute: Substitution cannot change a ground graph, because the graph contains no blanks to replace.
declarations.RDF11.ground_is_lean: Every ground graph is lean. All its instances equal the graph, so none can be a proper subgraph.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_comp: Two successive blank renamings of a graph equal one renaming by their composite function.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_of_fixes: A blank mapping fixing every blank that occurs in G leaves G unchanged; its behaviour on unused identities is irrelevant.
declarations.RDF11.mapBlank_is_instance: Every blank-to-blank mapping is a term substitution and therefore produces an instance.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism: An isomorphism supplies forward and inverse blank renamings, inverse on the blanks actually occurring in the graphs, with the forward image equal to H. IRIs and literals stay fixed. Unused ambient blank identities need not be bijective.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.inverse_image: Applying the inverse renaming to H gives exactly G. This follows from the forward image equality and the inverse law on G’s occurring blanks.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.mutual_instances: Isomorphic graphs are instances of one another, using the forward and inverse blank renamings.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.satisfies_iff: Every fixed simple interpretation satisfies G exactly when it satisfies an isomorphic H. The proof transports assignments in both directions.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.equivalent: Isomorphic graphs mutually entail each other. This is logical equivalence, not equality of their original blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.resourceDenot: Evaluate a term, keeping the result only if it belongs to IR. This is necessary because a blank assignment must be resource-valued and an arbitrary IRI may denote a property outside IR.
If a term is known to denote a resource r, resourceDenote returns precisely r.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.pullback: Assign each original blank the resource denoted by its replacement under A. Recompute every blank’s assignment, including identities also appearing in the image graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_pullba: If a substituted term denotes resource r, the original term denotes the same r under the pulled-back assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ordinary_trip: Truth of an instance of an ordinary triple implies truth of that original triple under the pulled-back assignment. Its predicate is an unchanged IRI; subject and object truth provide resource witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_substitution_entails: Every term-substitution image of an ordinary RDF graph entails the original. One assignment is pulled back for the entire graph. The image may use generalized syntax; the source must be ordinary.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_instance_entails: For two ordinary RDF graphs, if H is an instance of G then H simply entails G. The ordinary endpoint types exclude literal subjects and non-IRI predicates.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_instance_subgraph_equival: For ordinary graphs, a subgraph that is also an instance is logically equivalent to the original: subgraph entailment goes one way and instance entailment the other.
declarations.RDF11.instance_subgraph_entails: If a graph G contains an instance of ordinary E as a subgraph, then G entails E. This proves the sufficient direction of interpolation; the converse is not proved here.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration: A finite representation of set G carries a list, a no-duplicates proof, and a proof that list membership exactly matches G. An arbitrary plain list cannot satisfy this contract.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.unique: Remove repetitions from a finite list using decidable equality.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.unique_nodup: The list returned by unique has no duplicate elements.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.mem_unique: Removing repetitions preserves exactly which elements belong to the list.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.fromList: Convert any finite list into a certified enumeration of its represented set, removing repetitions and proving both membership and uniqueness.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.count_le_one: In a certified enumeration, every element occurs at most once.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.length_independent: Any two certified enumerations of the same set have equal lengths. Set size cannot depend on duplicated storage occurrences.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.repeated_input_same_se: Repeating an input element does not change the set represented by that input list.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.I: A two-resource interpretation used to distinguish separately witnessed graph truth from truth under a shared blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.triple: This example triple uses the shared blank as subject, a Boolean-selected IRI as predicate, and the fixed IRI false as object.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.graph: The singleton graph containing the selected example triple.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.witness_forced: Truth of this example triple forces its blank assignment to the resource selected by v.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.each_satisfiable: Each example graph is satisfiable separately, by choosing its own required blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.union_not_satisfied: The union is false in this interpretation because its shared blank would have to denote two different resources.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.merge_satisfied: The merge is true: its renamed blank domains permit independent resource witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.merge_does_not_entail: This countermodel proves that a merge does not in general entail the union with shared blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I: A simple interpretation with a property outside IR, permitted by the current literal reading of the source conditions; it exposes the generalized-predicate scope question.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.originalTriple: The generalized counterexample triple has a blank in predicate position.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.original: The singleton graph containing the generalized counterexample triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substitutedTriple: Replace the predicate blank by IRI p, keeping the subject and object IRI s.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substituted: The singleton graph containing that substituted triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.original_false: The original generalized graph is false in this interpretation: its predicate blank cannot be assigned the property outside IR.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substituted_true: With distinct s and p, the substituted graph is true in the counterexample interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.unrestricted_gene: The exhibited generalized instance does not entail its original under these truth conditions. This is evidence for a source-scope review question, not a declared W3C erratum.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IR: The resource domain, a set of elements of the ambient universe.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IR_nonempty: Evidence that the resource domain contains at least one element.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IP: The property domain. This field alone does not require IP to be a subset of IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IEXT: For each property, its extension is a set of ordered pairs of resources.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IS: An IRI denotes an element in the union of the resource and property domains.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IL: A literal may be undefined; when defined it denotes a resource.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.subject: Select the subject field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.predicate: Select the predicate field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.object: Select the object field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.subject: Select the subject field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.predicate: Select the predicate field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.object: Select the object field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.toFun: The forward map on blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.invFun: The inverse map on blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.left_inv: For every blank occurring in G, going forward and then back restores its identity.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.right_inv: For every blank occurring in H, going back and then forward restores its identity.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.image_eq: Renaming every blank in G with the forward map gives exactly H as a set of triples.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.triples: The finite list carrying the enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.nodup: Evidence that no element occurs twice in the enumeration list.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.membership: Evidence that list membership is equivalent to membership in the represented set.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Atom: A source atom records a half-open Unicode scalar interval and the claim or unresolved record IDs assigned to it.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Contains: Position i belongs to an atom if start ≤ i < stop.
declarations.Spec2Lean.ValidPartition: The atoms must cover the specified interval consecutively, with positive lengths, nonempty reference lists and only known record IDs. This is structural accountability, not semantic completeness.
declarations.Spec2Lean.partitionDecidable: Compute whether a finite atom list meets those partition conditions.
declarations.Spec2Lean.instDecidableValidPartition: Register the partition decision procedure so Lean can check concrete partitions using decide.
declarations.Spec2Lean.member_starts_after: Every atom in a valid partition starts at or after the partition’s initial boundary.
declarations.Spec2Lean.partition_sound: Every position inside a valid partition belongs to exactly one of its atoms. This proves there are no character-range gaps or overlaps.
declarations.Spec2Lean.references_grounded: Every atom in a valid partition has at least one reference, and each reference is a known ID. Known IDs include explicit unresolved records.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.ids: The allowed claim and unresolved record IDs for this concrete source snapshot.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mtSHA256: The recorded SHA-256 identifier of the archived Semantics bytes. Python verifies the hash; Lean does not prove the hash computation.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mtAtoms: The generated source-character partition for Semantics. Unextracted intervals are explicitly unresolved.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_valid: Lean checks that this concrete Semantics partition is structurally valid.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_all_positions: Every Unicode scalar position in the Semantics snapshot belongs to exactly one recorded interval.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_references: Every interval in the Semantics partition has nonempty, known references, including explicit unresolved references.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.conceptsSHA256: The recorded SHA-256 identifier of the archived Concepts bytes. Python verifies the hash; Lean does not prove the hash computation.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.conceptsAtoms: The generated source-character partition for Concepts. Unextracted intervals are explicitly unresolved.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_valid: Lean checks that this concrete Concepts partition is structurally valid.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_all_position: Every Unicode scalar position in the Concepts snapshot belongs to exactly one recorded interval.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_references: Every interval in the Concepts partition has nonempty, known references, including explicit unresolved references.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.Carrier: The canonical model’s carrier contains a tagged copy of every RDF term plus one dummy element. ULift places it in the arbitrary universe used by entailment. The dummy ensures a nonempty resource domain even when all term types are empty.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.encode: Embed an RDF term as a non-dummy element of the canonical carrier. Distinct terms retain distinct encodings.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.interpretation: Build a simple interpretation whose true relation pairs encode exactly the triples of G. Every carrier element is a resource and property in this particular model. IRIs and literals denote their own encodings. This choice does not constrain other simple interpretations.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.assignment: Assign each blank node its own term encoding. The exact-domain satisfaction lemma will discard unused assignments.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.denote_assignment: Every term denotes precisely its own encoding under the canonical interpretation and this blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.satisfies: The canonical interpretation satisfies G: each member triple witnesses its own relation membership.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.substitution: Decode a satisfying blank assignment back into term replacements. A dummy or missing denotation leaves a substitution entry unspecified; true triples cannot use the dummy in relation witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.decode_denotation: When a term denotes the encoding of v, replacing its blanks using the decoded assignment produces exactly v. Named terms stay fixed.
declarations.RDF11.Herbrand.true_triple_decodes: A triple true in the canonical interpretation decodes to a member of G, because every relation witness came from a G triple.
declarations.RDF11.entailment_has_instance_subgraph: If G entails E, its canonical model satisfies E. Decoding E’s shared assignment produces one substitution whose image is a subgraph of G. This necessary direction also works for generalized graphs.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_interpolation: For an ordinary RDF conclusion E, G entails E exactly when some instance of E is a subgraph of G. Necessity uses the canonical interpretation; sufficiency combines subgraph and ordinary instance entailment. Neither graph is assumed finite.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_interpolation_instances: Restate interpolation using the existing IsInstance predicate: there is a graph H that is an instance of E and a subgraph of G. The conclusion E is ordinary RDF.
declarations.RDF11.ground_entailment_iff_subset: A ground conclusion E is simply entailed exactly when every triple of E is already in G. Substitution cannot change a graph with no blanks, so interpolation reduces to membership inclusion.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.image: Map a certified finite enumeration through f, remove any resulting repetitions, and prove membership in the image set. Noninjective maps cannot create duplicate-bearing certified output.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteGraph: A graph is finite here when it has a certified enumeration: a finite list with exact membership and no repetitions. The general graph type remains an arbitrary set.
declarations.RDF11.finite_substitution: A finite graph stays finite after substitution. The existing enumeration image construction also handles triples that become identical.
declarations.RDF11.simple_compactness: If an arbitrary premise G entails a finite ordinary conclusion E, some finite subgraph H of G already entails E. Interpolation supplies H as an instance of E; its enumeration proves finiteness.
declarations.RDF11.Name: An RDF name is an IRI or a literal. The sum tags distinguish those two categories; blank nodes are not names.
declarations.RDF11.Term.names: An IRI contributes its IRI name. A literal contributes both itself and its syntactic datatype IRI. A blank contributes no name. The datatype projection must be supplied consistently with the eventual literal representation.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.names: A name occurs in a triple when one of its three terms contributes it, including datatype IRIs inside literals.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.vocabulary: The vocabulary of G is the set of names contributed by its member triples. Literal datatype IRIs are included via the explicit datatype projection.
declarations.RDF11.literal_contributes_two_names: Each abstract literal contributes both its own literal name and the name of its datatype IRI. They are distinct categories even if their textual representations resemble each other.
declarations.RDF11.Term.names_substitute: Substitution preserves all names already present in a term, because it replaces blanks and leaves names fixed.
declarations.RDF11.vocabulary_substitution: Every name of G still occurs in a substituted instance of G. The substitution may introduce additional names.
declarations.RDF11.vocabulary_subset: A subgraph’s vocabulary is a subset of the original graph’s vocabulary.
declarations.RDF11.entailment_vocabulary: Under simple semantics, every name in an entailed graph already occurs in the premise. The proof combines interpolation’s necessary direction, preservation of names by substitution, and subgraph vocabulary inclusion.
declarations.RDF11.fresh_iri_nonentailment: If E contains an IRI absent from G, then G does not simply entail E. Occurrence includes datatype IRIs inside literals; this theorem does not apply unchanged to stronger RDF/RDFS regimes.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization: Supply an IRI for each blank identity, with injectivity on blanks occurring in G and freshness against G’s vocabulary. Global freshness at creation remains external. The structure does not promise such a map exists for every abstract IRI domain.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.substitution: Turn the supplied skolem map into the existing simultaneous substitution, replacing each blank by its selected IRI.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.graph: The skolemized graph is exactly the set image of G under that substitution. No separate graph semantics is introduced.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.ground: The skolemized graph has no blank nodes: every occurring blank is replaced by an IRI.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.lean: The skolemized graph is lean because it is ground, reusing the existing ground-is-lean theorem.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.is_instance: The skolemized graph is an instance of the original graph by the existing definition of IsInstance.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.entails_original: For ordinary RDF G, its skolemization simply entails G. This follows directly from ordinary substitution entailment.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.contains_skolem_name: Every occurring original blank gives rise to its chosen skolem IRI somewhere in the image graph.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.original_not_entails: If G has at least one blank, it cannot simply entail its skolemization. Choose that blank’s fresh IRI and apply absent-IRI non-entailment. The nonempty-blank premise is essential.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.Avoids: H avoids the skolem vocabulary if it mentions none of the IRIs chosen for G’s occurring blanks, including mentions inside literal datatype positions.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.unname: If i is a chosen IRI for an occurring blank, recover such a blank; otherwise return no result. The injectivity condition makes recovery unique on used names.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.unname_name: Recovering the blank for an occurring blank’s skolem IRI returns that very blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverseTerm: Replace an IRI chosen for a source blank by that blank; leave other IRIs, all literals and existing blanks unchanged. This is used to transport interpolation witnesses back to G.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverseTriple: Apply the inverse-name map independently to all three terms of a triple.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverseTerm_fixed: A term that mentions no chosen skolem IRI is unchanged by the inverse-name map.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverseTerm_substitu: For a source term whose names are fresh and whose blanks occur in G, applying skolem substitution and then the inverse-name map recovers the original term.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverse_substituted_: Every original member triple is recovered exactly by unskolemizing its skolemized image. This uses both freshness and injectivity on occurring blanks.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverseSubstitution: Transform each resolved image of μ with the inverse-name map. The result is a new simultaneous substitution over the original blank identity domain.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.inverse_substitution: For a triple avoiding skolem IRIs, unskolemizing its substituted image equals applying the transformed substitution to the original triple. This is a scoped equality, not unrestricted commutation of arbitrary substitutions.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.conservative: For ordinary G and H, if H avoids the fresh skolem names, the skolemization entails H exactly when G entails H. One direction transports an interpolation witness through the inverse-name map; the other composes entailments. No finiteness or disjoint blank domains are assumed.
declarations.RDF11.SimplySatisfiable: G is simply satisfiable when some carrier and some simple interpretation on it satisfy G. The carrier universe is arbitrary but fixed for the proposition.
declarations.RDF11.SimplyUnsatisfiable: G is simply unsatisfiable when no simple interpretation satisfies it; this is the negation of SimplySatisfiable.
declarations.RDF11.simply_satisfiable: Every graph is simply satisfiable, by reusing the previously constructed one-element witness interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.never_simply_unsatisfiable: No graph is unsatisfiable under simple semantics, since every graph has the existing one-element model. Datatype-aware regimes can differ.
declarations.RDF11.SimplyValid: A process is modelled by its possible input/output pairs. It is simply valid when every permitted output is entailed by its corresponding input.
declarations.RDF11.SimplyInvalid: A process is simply invalid if it fails the universal truth-preservation condition. This does not prohibit the process or require applications to execute valid inferences.
declarations.RDF11.valid_composition: Composing two simply valid processes gives a simply valid process, by transitivity of entailment through the intermediate graph.
declarations.RDF11.subgraph_process_valid: Any process whose outputs are subgraphs of their inputs is simply valid.
declarations.RDF11.valid_under_extension: A simply valid process continues to preserve truth when interpretations are restricted by additional conditions. Separate syntax-admissibility restrictions remain separate obligations.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Relates: Express property-extension membership with ambient elements: p must be a property, x and y must be resources, and their ordered pair must belong to the existing typed IEXT(p).
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.RDFPropertyCo: The first RDF semantic condition says x is a property exactly when rdf:type relates x to the denotation of rdf:Property. The two vocabulary IRIs are parameters. This is one condition, not a full RDF interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_propertie: Under the first RDF property condition, every property is a resource: appearing as the subject of a true type pair requires membership in IR. This is derived under the condition rather than assumed for simple interpretations.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfD2_triple: Under the property condition, a true triple implies that its predicate is typed rdf:Property. The original predicate denotation supplies the property witness.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.generalized_t: If every property is a resource, the assignment pullback works for generalized predicates as well as subjects and objects. This extra hypothesis is explicit and is not assumed by ordinary instance entailment.
declarations.RDF11.propertyTypingImage: For each triple of G, produce the triple asserting its predicate has rdf:type rdf:Property; collect those results as a set.
declarations.RDF11.rdfD2_entailment: Every interpretation satisfying the first RDF property condition and G also satisfies its property-typing image. This proves the rule through the existing EntailsUnder relation.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_condition_substitution_entails: Under the first RDF property condition, any substitution image of a generalized graph entails its original. That condition supplies IP ⊆ IR, the hypothesis unavailable in unrestricted simple semantics.
declarations.RDF11.asciiLower: Convert ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase, preserving every other character. This uses the pinned Lean version's ASCII-only Char.toLower operation.
declarations.RDF11.LiteralSyntax: An interface exposing each literal's lexical string, datatype IRI and optional language tag. A literal has a tag exactly when its type is langString. Valid tags remain valid under ASCII lowercase conversion. Concrete syntax, equality and coverage of all legal forms remain separate obligations.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory: Fix one datatype theory across models: datatype identities, partial lexical-to-value functions, and injective string/tag pair values. Different IRIs may identify the same datatype. The exceptional language datatype has no L2V evaluation, represented by an everywhere-undefined partial evaluator; its actual value space is still the language-pair space.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.lexicalSpace: A string is in a datatype's lexical space exactly when its lexical-to-value function returns a value.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.valueSpace: The range of the ordinary partial lexical-to-value map. This helper alone is not the actual space of the exceptional language datatype; datatypeSpace selects its pair space instead.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.languageSpace: Language-string values are string/tag pairs with the tag normalized using US-ASCII lowercase rules. Valid raw tags may have mixed case; semantic tag values are lowercase, as RDF Concepts specifies.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.recognizedSpace: Look up an IRI’s identified datatype and use that datatype’s actual value space. Aliases of langString retain its pair space. Recognition in D is checked by callers.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.IllTyped: A literal is ill-typed relative to D when its ordinary datatype IRI is recognized and its lexical form has no lexical-to-value result. Language-tagged strings are handled separately.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.language_not_illTyp: A langString literal cannot satisfy the ill-typed predicate, because that predicate excludes the language-tagged special case.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.unrecognized_not_il: A datatype IRI absent from D cannot make its literal ill-typed under D. This does not impose application error-handling behavior.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization: Represent fixed external values inside a particular interpretation by a partial injective function. Distinct realized values cannot collapse. Values not needed by the recognized datatypes need not be present in every model carrier.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization.empty: The realization assigning no external values to the carrier. It supports the proof that recognizing no datatypes leaves all simple interpretations available.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.LiteralValue: The literal's IL denotation is defined and is the realization of the specified external value. Both parts refer to the same resource.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.DConditions: Conditions for D-interpretations include fixed denotation of every recognized datatype IRI, including langString. Recognized tagged literals denote normalized pairs; ordinary literals follow the identified datatype’s partial L2V evaluation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.DModel: A simple interpretation is a D-model when some partial injective value realization makes the D-conditions hold.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.dConditions_e: With no recognized datatype IRIs, neither branch of the datatype conditions can impose an obligation. The empty realization therefore works.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.dModel_empty: Every simple interpretation is a datatype interpretation for the empty recognition set, without enlarging its carrier.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.dConditions_r: If a model meets the datatype conditions for E and D is a subset of E, it also meets them for D, using the same external theory and realization.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.dModel_restri: Reducing the recognized datatype set preserves being a datatype model.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.illTyped_unde: An ill-typed literal has no IL denotation in a D-model. The proof uses the ordinary datatype condition and its failed lexical-to-value mapping.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.literalValue_: Two literals denoting the same realized external value have equal IL denotations. This is semantic equality, not equality of literal syntax.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.same_value_li: Recognized ordinary literals with the same lexical-to-value result denote the same resource, even if their datatype IRIs differ.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.recognized_li: A defined recognized literal realizes a value in its recognized datatype space. The tagged branch uses lowercase pair values; the ordinary branch uses the lexical-to-value range.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.literal_objec: Replacing an object literal by another with equal IL denotation preserves triple truth under the same blank-node assignment.
declarations.RDF11.DEntails: G D-entails E when every D-model satisfying G also satisfies E. The datatype theory and recognition set are fixed before quantifying over interpretations.
declarations.RDF11.DSatisfiable: A graph is D-satisfiable when at least one interpretation meets the D-conditions and satisfies the graph.
declarations.RDF11.DUnsatisfiable: A graph is D-unsatisfiable when it has no satisfying D-model.
declarations.RDF11.simple_implies_d_entailment: Every simple entailment remains valid when interpretations are restricted by datatype conditions.
declarations.RDF11.d_empty_iff_simple: Recognizing no datatype IRIs gives exactly simple entailment. Both implications are proved using the same interpretation carriers.
declarations.RDF11.d_entailment_monotone: Recognizing additional datatypes preserves entailments already valid with fewer recognized types, provided their external meanings stay fixed.
declarations.RDF11.illTyped_graph_unsatisfiable: A graph containing an ill-typed literal anywhere in a generalized triple has no D-model. This reuses the existing theorem that an undefined literal prevents graph truth.
declarations.RDF11.d_ex_falso: A graph with no D-model D-entails any conclusion: there is no satisfying premise interpretation that could refute the conclusion. This is not an application execution policy.
declarations.RDF11.d_literal_object_substitution: If a graph contains a triple with a recognized object literal, replacing that literal by a recognized ordinary literal with the same value yields a D-entailed triple. Different datatypes may supply the common value.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.relates_prope: A true semantic relation uses a member of IP as its property.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.relates_subje: The subject of a true semantic relation belongs to the resource universe IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.relates_objec: The object of a true semantic relation belongs to the resource universe IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_if: Triple truth is equivalent to defined denotations for all three terms and membership of the subject/object pair in the predicate relation. This connects ambient relation notation to typed IEXT witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_of: Build a triple-truth proof from its three denotation equations and the corresponding semantic relation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.iri_triple_tr: For an all-IRI triple, truth under any assignment is exactly the relation between its three IS denotations. Blank assignments are irrelevant.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.named_predica: For a triple with an IRI predicate, truth requires defined subject and object denotations related by that predicate's IS denotation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_unique: A term evaluated under one fixed assignment cannot have two different denotations. Rule soundness uses this to join shared terms across premises.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSymbol: Symbolic names for RDF vocabulary terms used in this reconstruction, including every positive container property. The constructor container n represents rdf:_(n+1), so the family is infinite.
declarations.RDF11.RDFVocabulary: Bind each RDF vocabulary symbol to an IRI, keeping distinct vocabulary spellings distinct. This does not require different IRIs to have different semantic denotations. Concrete string spellings remain an interface obligation.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSymbol.propertyAxiom: Select the RDF vocabulary symbols whose typing as rdf:Property is axiomatic, including every container property.
declarations.RDF11.RDFVocabulary.axioms: The full RDF axiom graph: the selected property typings and rdf:nil rdf:type rdf:List. It is a set, with an infinite container family and no finite cutoff.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.RDFConditions: Require the D-conditions, recognition of langString and xsd:string, the rdf:Property equivalence, complete realized datatype value spaces and their rdf:type equivalence, and every RDF axiom. Value realization connects the external value carrier to this interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.RDFModel: A simple interpretation is an RDF model when some value realization satisfies the complete RDFConditions conjunction for the fixed theory, D and vocabulary binding.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfModel_is_d: Every RDF model is a D-model for the same recognized datatype set. This supplies the semantic-extension link used by entailment proofs.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_value_spa: Every value in a recognized datatype's space is realized as a resource in an RDF model. Full realization and the rdf:type equivalence jointly establish this.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_literal_t: A recognized literal with a defined denotation has that denotation related by rdf:type to its datatype IRI's denotation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_disjoint_: No resource can belong to two disjoint recognized datatype value spaces. Both class memberships would realize one carrier element as two external values, contradicting injectivity and disjointness.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_axiom_tru: Every RDF axiom is true under any blank-node assignment and in any blank domain, since these axioms contain only IRIs.
declarations.RDF11.RDFEntails: G RDF-entails E when every RDF model of G is a model of E, using one fixed datatype theory, recognized set and vocabulary binding.
declarations.RDF11.RDFUnsatisfiable: An RDF-unsatisfiable graph has no satisfying RDF model.
declarations.RDF11.RDFVocabulary.baseDatatypes: The recognized set used by unqualified RDF entailment: exactly rdf:langString and xsd:string.
declarations.RDF11.d_implies_rdf_entailment: Datatype entailment remains valid after restricting models further by RDF's additional conditions and axioms.
declarations.RDF11.simple_implies_rdf_entailment: A simple entailment is also an RDF entailment, through the intervening D-model inclusion.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_empty_entails_axioms: The empty graph RDF-entails the entire RDF axiom graph, including its infinite container-property family.
declarations.RDF11.rdfD2: Every graph RDF-entails a graph typing each of its predicates as rdf:Property. This lifts the earlier property-condition proof to complete RDF models.
declarations.RDF11.rdfD1Conclusion: Construct the two-triple rdfD1 conclusion with one shared fresh blank. Existing blanks are placed in the left side of a disjoint sum; the new witness is on the right.
declarations.RDF11.rdfD1: A triple with a recognized literal entails the two-triple rdfD1 conclusion. The literal's actual denotation supplies one witness for both triples. An ill-typed premise has no satisfying model; no default value is invented.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_illTyped_unsatisfiable: The D-unsatisfiability proof for ill-typed literals also holds for RDF models because every RDF model is a D-model.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSSymbol: Symbolic names for the RDFS vocabulary together with all embedded RDF symbols. These are names, not separate classes of semantic objects.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSVocabulary: Bind the combined RDF/RDFS symbols injectively to IRIs. Semantic denotations may still coincide; concrete IRI-string validation is not implemented here.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSVocabulary.toRDF: Restrict a combined vocabulary binding to its RDF symbols, preserving distinctness. RDFS models use this exact binding in their inherited RDF conditions.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsDomainAxioms: The 16 property/domain pairs in the RDFS axiomatic-triples table. List membership is used only to describe this finite family; the resulting graph is a set.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsRangeAxioms: The 16 property/range pairs in the RDFS axiomatic-triples table, including Literal ranges for comment and label and List range for rdf:rest.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsHierarchyAxioms: The six explicit vocabulary hierarchy axioms: five subclass triples and isDefinedBy subproperty-of seeAlso.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsAxiomSymbols: Combine the finite domain, range and hierarchy families with all three axioms for every positive container index: type, Resource domain and Resource range.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSVocabulary.axioms: Turn each symbolic RDFS axiom into an all-IRI triple under the vocabulary binding, forming a set of triples.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ICEXT: The extension of class candidate y is exactly the set of x related to y by rdf:type. Class identity is not identified with this set, so distinct classes may have the same extension.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IC: The set of classes is the class extension of the denotation of rdfs:Class. Classes inhabit the same universe as other resources.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.LV: Literal values are the extension of rdfs:Literal. This is neither the set of literal syntax objects nor a definition equating LV to the range of IL.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.icext_resourc: Every member of a class extension is a resource, because it occurs as the subject of an rdf:type relation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.classes_are_r: Every member of IC is a resource. This follows by applying the class-extension resource theorem to rdfs:Class.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.RDFSCondition: Add the RDFS table to the inherited RDF conditions: Resource and tagged-literal extensions, datatype typing, domain/range, subclass/subproperty constraints, container/datatype consequences and all RDFS axioms. Ordinary datatype extensions are inherited from RDF.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.RDFSModel: An RDFS model has a value realization satisfying the combined RDF and RDFS conditions. It uses the same D and datatype meanings at both levels.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfsModel_is_: Every RDFS model is an RDF model for the inherited RDF vocabulary binding and the same D.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_property: The property set IP is exactly the class extension of rdf:Property. This follows from the inherited RDF property condition and the definition of ICEXT.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_datatype: A recognized datatype's class extension is its realized value space. For ordinary datatypes this is the range of L2V; the tagged special case uses normalized pair values.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_axiom_tr: Every RDFS axiom is true under any blank-node assignment. Its all-IRI form lets the proof transport the empty-domain axiom witness.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_iri_reso: Every IRI denotes an RDFS Resource. IS denotes a resource or property, RDF makes every property a resource, and the Resource extension is IR.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSEntails: G RDFS-entails E when every RDFS model satisfying G also satisfies E, with fixed datatype meanings, D and vocabulary binding.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_implies_rdfs_entailment: Every RDF entailment is an RDFS entailment for the same D, because the RDFS model class is a subset of the RDF model class. This is the model-theoretically supported direction.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_empty_entails_axioms: The empty graph RDFS-entails the whole RDFS axiom family, including all container indices.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep: A single instance of any of the 14 named RDFS rules, using triples from one premise graph. The syntax is generalized, so conclusions such as a literal subject remain expressible. Recognized datatypes supply rdfs1 even without a matching premise triple.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_step_sou: Every RDFS rule instance preserves truth under one fixed assignment. Shared terms across premises have the same denotation, so domain/range and hierarchy consequences combine the intended witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives: Derive triples from the premise, full RDF/RDFS axiom families, rdfD2, object-literal GrdfD1 and the RDFS rules. This general proof relation is distinct from Appendix A's conclusion-specific axiom seed.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_derivati: Induction on a derivation shows that every derived triple is true under the assignment satisfying the original premise graph. The proof composes axiom truth and single-step soundness.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_derives_entailment: If every triple of E has an RDFS derivation from G, then G RDFS-entails E. One assignment witnesses all derived triples, and the existing satisfaction theorem restricts it to E's actual blank domain.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSUnsatisfiable: An RDFS-unsatisfiable graph has no satisfying interpretation meeting the full RDFS conditions.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_disjoint_types_unsatisfiable: If the same term can be derived to have two recognized types with disjoint value spaces, the original graph has no RDFS model. This connects schema-rule derivations to datatype inconsistency rather than merely reporting incompatible labels.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs1: For every recognized datatype IRI d in D, entail d rdf:type rdfs:Datatype. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs2: From p rdfs:domain C and s p o, entail s rdf:type C. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs3: From p rdfs:range C and s p o, entail o rdf:type C. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs4a: From s p o, entail s rdf:type rdfs:Resource. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs4b: From s p o, entail o rdf:type rdfs:Resource. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs5: From p rdfs:subPropertyOf q and q rdfs:subPropertyOf r, entail p rdfs:subPropertyOf r. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs6: From p rdf:type rdf:Property, entail p rdfs:subPropertyOf p. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs7: From p rdfs:subPropertyOf q and s p o, entail s q o. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs8: From C rdf:type rdfs:Class, entail C rdfs:subClassOf rdfs:Resource. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs9: From C rdfs:subClassOf D and x rdf:type C, entail x rdf:type D. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs10: From C rdf:type rdfs:Class, entail C rdfs:subClassOf C. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs11: From C rdfs:subClassOf D and D rdfs:subClassOf E, entail C rdfs:subClassOf E. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs12: From p rdf:type rdfs:ContainerMembershipProperty, entail p rdfs:subPropertyOf rdfs:member. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSStep.rdfs13: From C rdf:type rdfs:Datatype, entail C rdfs:subClassOf rdfs:Literal. This constructor records the required premises; rdfs_step_sound proves the instance preserves truth.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.empty_graph_lemma: Headline review alias. If the empty graph entails E, then E has no triples. Otherwise the interpretation with empty property extensions would refute E while satisfying the empty premise. The one-line proof invokes empty_entails_only_empty without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.empty_graph_is_entailed: Headline review alias. Every graph entails the empty graph, which is true in every interpretation. The one-line proof invokes entails_empty without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.subgraph_lemma: Headline review alias. Every graph entails each of its subgraphs, because truth of every member triple implies truth of the selected subset. The one-line proof invokes subgraph_entailment without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.instance_lemma: Headline review alias. For two ordinary RDF graphs, if H is an instance of G then H simply entails G. The ordinary endpoint types exclude literal subjects and non-IRI predicates. The one-line proof invokes ordinary_instance_entails without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.merging_lemma: Headline review alias. I satisfies the merge exactly when I satisfies each graph separately. The separate assignments combine because the renamed blank domains are disjoint. The one-line proof invokes satisfies_merge without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.interpolation_lemma: Headline review alias. Restate interpolation using the existing IsInstance predicate: there is a graph H that is an instance of E and a subgraph of G. The conclusion E is ordinary RDF. The one-line proof invokes ordinary_interpolation_instances without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.compactness: Headline review alias. If an arbitrary premise G entails a finite ordinary conclusion E, some finite subgraph H of G already entails E. Interpolation supplies H as an instance of E; its enumeration proves finiteness. The one-line proof invokes simple_compactness without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.isomorphism_invariance: Headline review alias. Every fixed simple interpretation satisfies G exactly when it satisfies an isomorphic H. The proof transports assignments in both directions. The one-line proof invokes GraphIsomorphism.satisfies_iff without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.skolemization_lemma: Headline review alias. For ordinary G and H, if H avoids the fresh skolem names, the skolemization entails H exactly when G entails H. One direction transports an interpolation witness through the inverse-name map; the other composes entailments. No finiteness or disjoint blank domains are assumed. The one-line proof invokes Skolemization.conservative without changing its hypotheses or scope.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.Carrier: The witness model has one distinct carrier element for every external datatype value, plus one unnamed resource. ULift places the construction in any chosen universe; this is not a restriction on all D-models.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.embed: Place an external datatype value into its own carrier element in the witness model.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.unnamed: The extra resource used for unconstrained names and blank-node witnesses. It is not a fallback denotation for recognized ill-typed literals.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.realization: Realize every external value injectively in the witness carrier. This particular model can contain all values even though D-models in general are not required to do so.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal: Choose IL values for the witness model: unrecognized types denote the unnamed resource; recognized tagged strings denote normalized pairs; recognized ordinary literals follow L2V, retaining undefined results.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.interpretation: Construct a simple interpretation with IR and IP equal to the whole witness carrier and every property extension full. Every recognized IRI, including langString, denotes its fixed datatype; literal evaluation follows the existing datatype rules. This is an existence witness, not a constraint on every interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.language_none: A literal whose datatype differs from langString cannot have a language tag, by the literal-syntax interface's tagged-iff condition.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.conditions: Prove that the constructed interpretation meets every D-condition, including the behavior of ill-typed literals that do not occur in the graph being studied.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.model: Package the witness interpretation and its injective realization as a D-model.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal_defined: Every literal that is not ill-typed under D has a defined denotation in the witness model. The proof separates unrecognized, tagged and ordinary recognized cases.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.assignment: Assign every blank identity the same unnamed resource in this witness model. The satisfaction proof later restricts the assignment to the blanks occurring in the graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.term_defined: If a term contains no ill-typed literal, its denotation under the witness assignment is a resource. This covers IRIs, literals and blank nodes uniformly.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeModel.satisfies: The witness interpretation satisfies every graph with no ill-typed literal occurrences: all terms denote and all property pairs are present. The graph may be infinite.
declarations.RDF11.d_satisfiable_iff_no_illTyped: A graph has a D-model exactly when none of its triples contains an ill-typed literal. One direction uses undefined-literal falsity; the other constructs an explicit model. This concerns simple D-semantics, not all RDF/RDFS constraints.
declarations.RDF11.d_unsatisfiable_iff_illTyped: A graph is D-unsatisfiable exactly when some member triple contains an ill-typed literal. This is the full characterization, not merely the already-proved sufficient condition.
declarations.RDF11.empty_d_satisfiable: The empty graph has a D-model for every fixed external datatype theory and recognized set D. Empty here describes the graph, not the recognition set.
declarations.RDF11.d_entailment_not_simple_of_illType: Given an ill-typed literal, construct two ordinary singleton graphs: the premise has that literal as object; the conclusion instead has an IRI object. The premise D-entails the conclusion by unsatisfiability, but does not simply entail it by ground interpolation. The existence of an ill-typed literal remains an explicit hypothesis.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.RecognizedValue: Record a defined value for a recognized literal, either a normalized tagged-string pair or a successful ordinary lexical-to-value result. No value is assigned by this relation to an ill-typed or unrecognized literal.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.recognizedVal: Every recognized-value witness gives the corresponding IL denotation in any D-model, by the appropriate datatype condition.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.equal_recogni: Two literals with recognized-value witnesses for the same external value have equal IL denotations. Tagged and ordinary values may be compared in the shared value carrier.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapLiteral: Apply one map to literals while preserving IRI names and blank-node identities.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapLiteral: Apply the same literal map simultaneously to all three positions of a generalized triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapLiteral: Take the set image of all graph triples under the literal map. If different triples become identical, they form one member, not repeated entries.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_mapLit: A term's denotation is unchanged when every literal it contains is replaced by one with the same IL denotation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ma: Value-preserving literal replacement preserves truth of a generalized triple under the same blank assignment, including replacement in subject or predicate position.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_map: Replacing occurring literals by equal-denotation literals preserves graph satisfaction in both directions. One assignment witnesses the whole graph; restriction to its exact blank domain is reused from the existing satisfaction theorem.
declarations.RDF11.ValuePreservingLiteralMap: On every literal occurring in G, the map either leaves the literal unchanged or supplies recognized-value witnesses showing that old and new literals have one common value.
declarations.RDF11.value_preserving_literal_map_satis: Any literal map meeting the value-preservation contract leaves graph satisfaction unchanged in every D-model of the fixed theory.
declarations.RDF11.d_literal_map_equivalent: A graph and its simultaneous value-preserving literal image D-entail one another. The proof covers all literal positions and does not assume finite graphs or disjoint datatype spaces.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.GrdfD1_triple: A true triple containing a recognized literal gives the literal's rdf:type membership as a generalized triple. This semantic helper covers any position; the named Appendix A rule and closure use its object-literal specialization.
declarations.RDF11.literalTypingImage: Collect the generalized typing triples obtained from recognized object literals in G, exactly the object-position premise of GrdfD1.
declarations.RDF11.GrdfD1: An RDF graph entails all the generalized literal typings in its GrdfD1 image. If a premise literal is ill-typed, there is no satisfying RDF model; the rule needs no separate well-typedness assumption.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives.rdfD2: Extend a derivation by typing the predicate of an already-derived triple as rdf:Property.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives.GrdfD1: Extend a derivation by typing an already-derived recognized object literal with its datatype IRI, preserving the literal in generalized subject position.
declarations.RDF11.NonContainerAxioms: Select axioms containing no container membership IRI. Name occurrence uses the existing vocabulary definition, including an embedded literal datatype IRI.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerAxioms: Select axioms containing the specified container IRI. Index zero denotes rdf:_1 under the vocabulary binding.
declarations.RDF11.ConclusionAxioms: Select container axioms using container IRIs occurring in conclusion E. This deliberately follows the printed E-only selection rather than using G or the union of both graphs.
declarations.RDF11.AxiomSeed: Form the seed from G, non-container axioms and E-selected container axioms. Add rdf:_1 axioms if the selected axioms add no new triples to the preceding seed. This is the literal set-growth reading of the printed fallback.
declarations.RDF11.axiomSeed_contains: The seed retains every original premise triple.
declarations.RDF11.axiomSeed_subset: Every seed triple is either an original premise triple or an actual axiom. Thus even the conditional fallback cannot introduce a non-axiomatic assertion.
declarations.RDF11.RDFStep: One generalized RDF inference step: predicate typing by rdfD2 or recognized object-literal typing by GrdfD1. Neither rule invents blank nodes.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSGeneralizedStep: A generalized RDFS step may use either generalized RDF rule or any of the 14 RDFS rules, with one shared premise graph.
declarations.RDF11.RuleDerives: The inductive closure of a seed under a specified rule relation. A rule application requires derivations for its supporting graph. This is a mathematical proof relation, not an executable saturation algorithm.
declarations.RDF11.ruleDerives_least: Every set containing the seed and closed under the rules contains all RuleDerives consequences. This establishes the least-closure property of the inductive specification.
declarations.RDF11.RDFClosure: Appendix A's generalized RDF closure towards E: the specified axiom seed saturated by rdfD2 and GrdfD1, recognizing exactly langString and xsd:string. Finite generation and completeness are separate obligations.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSClosure: The corresponding generalized RDFS closure adds both axiom families to the selected seed and permits the RDF and RDFS rules. It uses the source's conclusion-specific container selection and base datatype set.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_step_soun: Each generalized RDF rule preserves truth under one fixed assignment in an RDF model. The proof reuses the existing rdfD2 and literal-typing theorems.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_generali: Both RDF and RDFS branches of the generalized rule relation preserve truth under the same assignment in an RDFS model.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.axiomSeed_tru: If G and the axioms are true under an assignment, the selected seed is true under that assignment, independently of which fallback branch applies.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ruleDerives_t: Truth of the seed and truth preservation by every rule imply truth of the entire inductive closure under one fixed assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_closure_s: Within RDF models, G and its conclusion-specific closure have exactly the same satisfaction status. This does not assert that simple entailment from that closure detects every RDF consequence.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_closure_: Within RDFS models, the specified closure preserves and reflects satisfaction of G. The separate completeness claim about a simple-entailment check is not proved here.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_closure_simple_check_sound: If the generalized RDF closure simply entails E, then G RDF-entails E. This proves the positive direction without requiring consistency or finite inputs.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_closure_simple_check_sound: If the generalized RDFS closure simply entails E, then G RDFS-entails E. The converse remains open.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_closure_instance_check_sound: If an instance of E is a subgraph of the RDF closure, G RDF-entails E. The proof uses RDF's property-resource condition to justify generalized-instance entailment.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_closure_instance_check_sound: The same instance-subgraph check is sound for RDFS closure. It composes seed/rule soundness with the already-proved generalized substitution result.
declarations.RDF11.container_membership_derivable: Derive generic rdfs:member membership from an indexed membership assertion using that index's full RDFS axiom, rdfs12 and rdfs7. Every positive container index is covered.
declarations.RDF11.container_membership_entailment: Every indexed container membership assertion RDFS-entails the corresponding generic membership assertion. The theorem uses the full semantic axiom family, not the restricted closure seed.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.mapBlank: Rename a blank subject or graph-name key while fixing an IRI. The result remains an IRI-or-blank subject, so literals cannot become graph names.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.toTerm_mapBlank: Embedding a subject into the general term type commutes with blank renaming; the ordinary and generalized syntactic views agree.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.mapBlank_comp: Two successive blank renamings of a subject equal their function composition.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.mapBlank_id: The identity blank renaming leaves each subject or graph-name key unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.mapBlank_of_fixes: A renaming that fixes the blank, if any, occurring in a subject leaves that subject unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.mapBlank: Rename the blank identities of an ordinary RDF triple, retaining its IRI predicate and ordinary subject/object categories.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize_mapBlank: Renaming an ordinary triple and then viewing it as generalized equals first generalizing and then renaming.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize_injective: Two ordinary triples with equal generalized views are equal; generalization forgets no ordinary triple information.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.mapBlank: Rename every triple of an ordinary graph by set image. Coincident image triples remain one set member.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize_mapBlank: Ordinary graph renaming commutes with the embedding into generalized graphs, connecting dataset graphs to the existing graph proofs.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize_injective: Equality of generalized views implies equality of ordinary graphs, because both the triple embedding and graph sets are extensional.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.mapBlank_comp: Two ordinary graph renamings equal a single renaming by the composed function.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.mapBlank_of_fixes: A renaming that fixes every blank occurring in an ordinary graph leaves the graph unchanged; unused blank identities impose no condition.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.mapBlank_id: The identity renaming leaves an ordinary graph unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.hasBlank_mapBlank: A blank occurs in a renamed term exactly when it is the image of an original occurring blank.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.hasBlank_mapBlan: A blank occurs anywhere in a renamed generalized triple exactly when some original occurring blank maps to it.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.hasBlank_mapBlank: The blank identities of a graph image are exactly the images of its original occurring blanks, including when a noninjective map merges occurrences.
declarations.RDF11.GraphName: Dataset graph names use the same IRI-or-blank alternatives as ordinary subjects. A literal is not a graph name.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset: An RDF dataset has one unnamed default graph and a partial lookup from graph names to ordinary graphs. A single blank type is shared by keys and all contents; present empty graphs remain distinct from missing keys. Different names may hold equal graphs.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.HasNamedGraph: The dataset contains the named pair consisting of this graph name and this exact graph, including an empty graph.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.name_unique: Two graphs associated with the same name in one dataset are equal. Name uniqueness follows from the functional representation.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.hasBlank: A blank occurs in a dataset if it occurs in the default graph, in any present named graph, or as a present graph-name key. An empty graph with a blank name still contributes that blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.HasName: This graph name is present in the dataset, regardless of whether its associated graph has any triples.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.quads: Project the named graphs to name/triple membership. This deliberately records no membership for an empty named graph and omits the separately represented default graph.
